---
title: "Is student math final grade a function of family size?"
---

## Data Origins

- [Student Performance Dataset - UCI Machine Learning Repository](https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/320/student%2Bperformance)
- File: [student-mat.csv](student-mat.csv)
- Dependent Variable: final mathematics grade (integer, 0-20)
- Independent Variable: student family size (boolean, whether or not > 3)

## Analysis & Conclusion

```{python}
#| label: tbl-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Final mathematics grade by family size"
#| echo: false

import pandas as pd
students = pd.read_csv("student-mat.csv", sep=";")
summary = (
    students.groupby("famsize")["G3"]
    .agg(
        n="count",
        mean="mean",
        sd="std"
    )
    .round(2)
    .rename_axis("Family size")
    .reset_index()
    .rename(columns={"n": "N", "mean": "Mean", "sd": "SD"})
)

summary.style.hide(axis="index").format({
    "Mean": "{:.2f}",
    "SD": "{:.2f}",
})
```


```{python}
#| echo: false

import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats

students = pd.read_csv("student-mat.csv", sep=";")

summary = (
    students.groupby("famsize")["G3"]
    .agg(["count", "mean", "std"])
)

summary

le3 = students.loc[students["famsize"] == "LE3", "G3"]
gt3 = students.loc[students["famsize"] == "GT3", "G3"]

test = stats.ttest_ind(le3, gt3, equal_var=False)

test

print("Results: ")
print(f"t = {test.statistic:.2f}")
print(f"df = {test.df:.2f}")
print(f"p = {test.pvalue:.3f}")
```
___
At the α = .05 significance level, the result failed to reject the null hypothesis. The Welch two-sample t-test did not find a statistically significant difference in final mathematics grades between the two family-size groups, *t*(231.57) = 1.69, *p* = .092. Although students in the `LE3` group had a mean final grade 0.82 points higher than students in the `GT3` group, the evidence is insufficient to conclude that mean final mathematics grade differs by family size.
